subject.title: Codex PreToolUse native hook relay spawns CPU-bound openclaw-hooks processes and stalls gateway RPC

question: Should OpenClaw fix the default relay architecture by making remaining hooks lightweight and pre-spawn bounded, or use operator-configurable relay policy as the primary mitigation?
rationale: The availability defect is established, but architectural cost removal preserves the default safety contract while an opt-out or event policy adds compatibility-sensitive configuration and shifts responsibility to operators.

options.title: Lightweight bounded relay
options.body: Retain required native gating hooks while eliminating full-runtime startup cost and bounding concurrency before expensive execution.

options.title: Configurable relay policy
options.body: Expose enabled events or an opt-out, accepting a new configuration surface and operator responsibility for disabled policy coverage.

options.title: Disable relay by default
options.body: Make native relay opt-in, reducing overhead but changing existing approval, loop-detection, and diagnostic behavior.

recommendation.title: Lightweight bounded relay
recommendation.body: Retain required native gating hooks while eliminating full-runtime startup cost and bounding concurrency before expensive execution.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the current Codex harness boundary and is the strongest history-based candidate to choose its permanent default and compatibility contract.
